newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed up 0.05 rupees at 41.20 to the dollar in the kerb market on Monday, with dealers expecting the rupee to open flat on renewed U.S. dollar demand.
They said the dollar regained some lost ground amid fresh buying after the rupee opened at 41.12 against the dollar.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate was unchanged at 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar, set on October 22.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed unchanged at 3.0 percent.
